newsitem.title: UK: London police question man about IRA bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: London police question man about IRA bomb attack.

text.p: British police have arrested a suspected IRA guerrilla in connection with the deadly bomb attack in London's Docklands that ended the IRA's ceasefire in February 1996, British security sources said on Thursday.

"A man has been arrested by the Metropolitan Police in connection with terrorist offences and is currently in custody at a London police station," a London police spokeswoman said. "He is being interviewed by anti-terrorist officers."
The bomb in London's Docklands business district killed two people and marked the end of a 17-month ceasefire by Irish Republican Army guerrillas fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland.
Security sources said the man was among seven people arrested on Saturday in a raid on a farmhouse near Crosmaglen in Northern Ireland. He was flown to London early on Thursday, they said.

Three of the men arrested in the raid were later released, while three were ordered to be held in custody on Thursday in Northern Ireland, accused of plotting murder, belonging to the IRA and having sniper weapons.

One of them, 39-year-old Martin McGinn, was ordered to be held in custody on three guerrilla murder counts, including that of killing 23-year-old Stephen Restorick, a British soldier shot by a sniper in February.
McGinn, from the Irish town of Castleblaney, denied the charges and other guerrilla crimes at court in Banbridge, County Down, south of Belfast.

Restorick was killed by a single shot as he talked to a motorist at a security checkpoint near Bessbrook army base in County Armagh, known as "bandit country" for its history of attacks on British forces.
Restorick was the second soldier killed by the IRA since it abandoned its truce.
